title: A residual frame cover makes lisse lattices Kummer tame
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its norm topology, valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On each scheme $Z$, use the pullbacks $A_{E,Z}$ and $A_{\mathcal O_E,Z}$ of the condensed continuous-map rings of $E$ and $\mathcal O_E$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and internal module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Lisse means pro-etale locally finite free, allowing rank zero [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. Let $S$ be a nonempty connected separated finite-type $k$-scheme and let $M_0$ be a lisse finite-rank $A_{\mathcal O_E,S}$-module. Put $M=A_{E,S}\otimes_{A_{\mathcal O_E,S}}M_0$.

There is a connected finite etale surjection $c:H\to S$ [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism] such that $c^*(M_0/\varpi M_0)$ is constant, and with the following property. For every regular separated finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$ and reduced strict normal crossings boundary $D\subset Y$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], put $W=Y\setminus D$. For every $g:W\to S$ admitting a factorization through $H$, the lisse rational module $g^*M$ becomes constant on the prime-to-$p$ parameter-root tower at each geometric point of $Y$: if $R$ is the strict henselization of its local ring and $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ are regular parameters defining the components of $D$, its pullback to
$$\varprojlim_{(n,p)=1}\operatorname{Spec}\left(R[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_1^n-t_1,\ldots,x_r^n-t_r)\right)[1/(t_1\cdots t_r)]$$
is a finite free constant $A_E$-module. The limit uses the divisibility transition maps sending each higher root to the appropriate power; the constant module means the coefficient sheaf tensored with a finite-dimensional $E$-vector space. Strict henselization has the meaning of [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. The assertion holds for every choice of the parameters. The case $r=0$ is included and the tower is then the identity. No properness or generation assertion is included.

source.place: Agent-formulated consequence of Proposition 6.8.4 (integral lisse sheaves and their compatible finite etale reductions), pp.59-60, and ILO IX Proposition 2.1, printed pp.133-134 (parameter-root trivialization). Use the finite cover trivializing reduction modulo varpi; all later congruence monodromy groups are ell-groups. The exact internal pulled-coefficient formulation is a consequence, not a verbatim quoted theorem.

proof.text: Write $A=\mathcal O_E$, $A_n=A/\varpi^n$ and $F_n=M_0/\varpi^nM_0$. First identify the pulled condensed coefficient rings with the continuous-function coefficient sheaves, naturally for $A\to A_n$ and $A\to E$, by lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-realizations. Pass between internal modules and sheaf modules using def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence; its underlying sheaf is unchanged, so finite free local trivializations are unchanged. By lem-sfb-integral-lisse-reduction-equivalence, $(F_n)$ is a tower of finite locally free $A_n$-sheaves with $F_{n+1}/\varpi^nF_{n+1}\cong F_n$. By det-pe-finite-local-systems-twist every $F_n$ comes from an etale finite locally constant module sheaf. Thus the finite-coefficient correspondence may be applied to these actual reductions, rather than to a different coefficient model.

Apply lem-weil-pbc-finite-set-monodromy-torsor to the underlying finite locally constant set sheaf of $F_1$ on the nonempty connected scheme $S$. It gives a connected finite etale surjection $c:H\to S$ on which that set sheaf is constant. In cor-galois-lisse-representations(1), a trivial action on the underlying set is exactly a trivial action on the module; hence $c^*F_1$ is a constant $A_1$-module sheaf. Its fibre is finite free of some rank $d\geq0$, because $F_1$ is locally free. This is the sole choice of $H$; it depends only on $M_0$, and no later boundary pair enters its construction.

source.place: Section Tag 03SF (section-finite-etale-under-galois); finite module structures by the fibre equivalence, with Stacks 0DV5 and 0DV6 for the finite-set torsor

proof.text: Fix any pair $(Y,D)$, any factorization $W\to H\to S$ of $g$, any geometric point of $Y$, and any of the parameter choices in the statement. Write $R$ for the strict henselization, $f=\prod_i t_i$, and $U=\operatorname{Spec}R[1/f]$. The original local ring is Noetherian regular; lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian and lem-sc-strict-henselization-regular show the same for $R$. Its characteristic is $p$. The parameters $t_i$ in the statement are part of a regular system of parameters in $R$. By lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization they are nonzero prime elements in a domain; thus $U$ is a nonempty integral, hence connected, affine scheme (also when $r=0$, $f=1$). Let $N$ be the pullback of $M_0$ to $U$. Exact Cartesian coefficient pullback, sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients(1), preserves its finite free local models and identifies $N/\varpi^nN$ with $F_n|_U$. In particular $N/\varpi N\cong(A_1)_U^d$, since the map factors through $H$.

source.place: Tags 06LJ (lemma-henselization-noetherian), 06LN (lemma-henselization-regular); ILO IX 2.1 strict-local setup, p.133

proof.text: For each $n\geq1$ consider $K_n=\ker(\operatorname{GL}_d(A_n)\to\operatorname{GL}_d(A_1))$. The finite local rings and surjective transition maps are those of lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients, and the residue field $\kappa=A_1$ is finite by lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr. It has characteristic $\ell$: $|\ell|_E<1$ puts $\ell$ in the maximal ideal, so the field characteristic divides the prime $\ell$. Filter $K_n$ by $K_{n,i}=1+\varpi^i\operatorname{Mat}_d(A_n)$ for $1\leq i\leq n$, with $K_{n,n}=1$. The map $1+\varpi^i B\mapsto B\bmod\varpi$ identifies $K_{n,i}/K_{n,i+1}$ with the additive group $\operatorname{Mat}_d(\kappa)$: multiplication is addition modulo $\varpi^{i+1}$, and cancellation of $\varpi^i$ is valid in the DVR before taking the quotient. These groups have order $|\kappa|^{d^2}$, a power of $\ell$. Multiplying the successive orders shows $K_n$ is an $\ell$-group. This includes $n=1$ and $d=0$, when it is trivial.

source.place: Agent matrix-filtration calculation for the finite reductions of Proposition 6.8.4(1); uses the DVR and finite residue-field facts explicitly cited

proof.text:
Choose a geometric point of $U$. For each $n$, $N/\varpi^nN$ is a pro-etale local system of finite $A_n$-modules on $U$, so det-pe-finite-local-systems-twist on $U$ writes it as $
u_U^*$ of an etale local system of finite $A_n$-modules, with $
u_U^*,
u_{U,*}$ quasi-inverse; constancy may therefore be tested on this etale model and transported back, also after pullback to the covers below. cor-galois-lisse-representations(1) associates to this etale model its finite free $A_n$-fibre $B_n$ and its continuous monodromy action. The rank of $B_n$ is $d$, since reduction to $A_1$ is the free rank-$d$ fibre in step 3; scalar compatibility in that correspondence identifies its residual action with the trivial action. After a choice of basis, the image $Q_n$ is therefore a subgroup of $K_n$, so its order is a power of $\ell$ and is prime to $p$. Apply thm-galois-fundamental to the finite continuous $\pi_1(U)$-set $Q_n$ with left translation via the image quotient. Right translations $g\cdot q=qg^{-1}$ commute with this action and make the corresponding finite etale cover $P_n	o U$ a $Q_n$-torsor. Base change to it restricts monodromy to the kernel of the image map, so $N/\varpi^nN$ becomes the constant free $A_n$-module on $P_n$. Only this actual monodromy group is used; the order of an arbitrary trivializing cover would not suffice.

source.place: Tag 03SF (section-finite-etale-under-galois), image quotient and its regular finite action; theorem-fundamental-group and its base-change clause

proof.text: Apply lem-sfb-strict-local-prime-to-p-kummer-splitting to $R$, the chosen $t_i$, and the torsor $P_n$ with group $Q_n$. Its hypotheses hold by steps 3 and 5. Obtain a positive integer $m_n$ prime to $p$ such that $P_n$ is trivial over the punctured $m_n$-root scheme. The full prime-to-$p$ parameter-root tower $T$ in the item has a projection to this scheme. A section of the trivialized torsor therefore pulls back to a section over $T$; pullback of the trivialization on $P_n$ along this section gives $(N/\varpi^nN)|_T\cong(A_n)_T^d$. Exact Cartesian coefficient pullback identifies this sheaf with $N_T/\varpi^nN_T$, where $N_T=N|_T$. No common finite root order for all $n$ is required.

source.place: Expose IX Proposition 2.1 and its finite simultaneous parameter-root normal form, printed pp.133-134; application at each finite monodromy quotient

proof.text: Choose these finite-level trivializations compatibly, as follows. Fix one at level $1$. Suppose one is fixed at level $n$ and choose any at level $n+1$. Its reduction differs from the fixed one by an automorphism of $(A_n)_T^d$, hence by an invertible matrix of sections. By lem-sfb-totally-disconnected-coefficient-realization for finite discrete sets, it is a continuous locally constant function $|T|\to\operatorname{GL}_d(A_n)$. Every invertible matrix over $A_n$ lifts to one over $A_{n+1}$: lift its entries, and the determinant remains a unit because its reduction modulo the maximal ideal is nonzero. Choose a lift for each element of the finite set $\operatorname{GL}_d(A_n)$; this set map is continuous between discrete sets. Composing with the matrix function gives a lifted automorphism on $T$. Adjusting the level-$n+1$ trivialization by this lift makes its reduction the chosen level-$n$ one. Induction gives an isomorphism of the whole reduction tower with $((A_n)_T^d)_n$. This argument does not assume that taking a constant sheaf commutes with inverse limits, or that $T$ is connected.

source.place: Agent compatible-basis construction for Proposition 6.8.4(1); finite constant coefficient sections as in Lemma 4.2.12

proof.text:
The pullback $N_T$ is lisse and its reductions are the actual tower in step 7, by exact Cartesian pullback. Apply lem-sfb-integral-lisse-reduction-equivalence on the scheme $T$ itself. Full faithfulness of reduction takes the compatible tower isomorphism of step 7 to $N_T\cong(A_T)^d$, since the latter has reduction tower $((A_n)_T^d)_n$. Rationalizing this isomorphism, using the inverse-image tensor comparison $t$ of def-sfb-condensed-pullback-tensor-comparison for $g^*M=g^*(A_{E,S}\otimes_{A_{\mathcal O_E,S}}M_0)$ and the Cartesian coefficient isomorphisms of sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients(1) for $A_E$ and $A_{\mathcal O_E}$, gives
$$ (g^*M)|_T\cong E_T\otimes_{A_T}N_T\cong(E_T)^d. $$
Returning through the coefficient realization and the internal-module equivalence of step 1 yields exactly the constant $A_E$-module associated to $E^d$ in the statement. The argument applied to an arbitrary point and parameter tuple, so proves the assertion for every such choice. If $r=0$, the geometric splitting lemma uses $m_n=1$ and the same proof runs on $\operatorname{Spec}R$; if $d=0$, all bases and matrices are empty and the result is the zero module.

The item statement is unchanged. In live and side-live the item is still unsplit, it is not dropped and it has no re-split note; this is a first split. The proof is sound: one residual cover H from the finite-set monodromy torsor; the congruence kernel K_n is an ℓ-group (filtration quotients Mat_d(κ), char κ = ℓ); the image Q_n ⊂ K_n gives a Q_n-torsor P_n; the new node splits P_n at a finite root level m_n prime to p; compatible bases are built by lifting GL_d and the lattice is rebuilt on the tower T by the integral lisse equivalence. No uniform root level is needed, which is correct because infinite tame image is allowed. The new node is true: a prime-to-p group forces tameness (no wild inertia, no inseparability, no defect), and Abhyankar gives π1^t = ∏Ẑ'(1)^r, abelian, so the cover splits at n = exponent of G. I tested r=0, a strictly henselian DVR with G = Z/ℓ, G = S_3 with p ≥ 5, and disconnected P; G = Z/p is correctly excluded. It is not a duplicate: the snc-tame-root-etale and finite-fibre nodes assume the splitting it proves, and lem-per-snc-parameter-root-quotient gives only a normal form; its future splitter should cite that node or Stacks pione Abhyankar, not SGA 1 XIII 5.3.
